title: Route PDFs, Office files and images to the right parser in /v1/scrape (Content-Type plus magic bytes)
summary: After any driver returns bytes, sniff Content-Type and then the first bytes (%PDF-, a zip containing [Content_Types].xml, OLE compound file, PNG/JPEG/WebP). If the body is not HTML, hand the already-fetched bytes to the matching parser in quarry-transform (pdf.rs, docx.rs, images.rs) instead of running charset decoding and readability over binary data, and record the detected kind in output metadata. Express it as a typed Replan::IsFile when the planner work in R-t2-03-06 lands.
whyItMatters: PDFs and Office files linked from sites are a common knowledge-base input. Today a PDF URL goes through readability and produces garbage markdown that users notice immediately, even though a PDF text extractor already exists.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (firecrawl), unique; table-stakes for a Firecrawl-class scraper
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: kind = sniff(content_type) or sniff_magic(first 512 bytes): %PDF-, PK zip with [Content_Types].xml, OLE compound file, PNG/JPEG/WebP. If kind is not html, raise AddFeature(pdf|document|image) carrying the already-downloaded bytes as prefetch so the parser needs no refetch. Record kind in output metadata.

title: Turn on the LLM browser planner by default, with budgets, a browsing procedure prompt and connector-first routing
summary: Replace the QUARRY_BROWSER_AGENT_LLM env gate with an org-policy flag so the planner in execution-core is the default AI browser loop, with per-run step, time and token budgets. Add a versioned browsing procedure to the planner prompt (observe, act, re-observe; escalation ladder AX ref -> semantic locator -> set-of-marks -> coordinates; stop rules) and a routing step that prefers Integration Plane provider actions or Quarry search/scrape before opening a browser, unless the user asked for the browser.
whyItMatters: This is the AI-browser feature users actually see; without an enabled planner the in-app browser has no real agent. A procedure prompt raises task success at near-zero cost, and connector-first routing is cheaper, more reliable and honours provider OAuth scopes.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (FE098 hosted interact loop: capped interactive snapshot, one tool, step caps and guardrails) for the loop; Aside for the procedure prompt; Codex for connector-first routing
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Loop 2 of 3 (common); procedure prompt 2 of 3 (table-stakes); connector-first 1 of 3 (unique to Codex)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Loop: interactive snapshot (capped around 40k chars) plus URL goes to the LLM with one tool; execute; return a snapshot diff; stop on done, step cap or budget; guardrails reject commands outside the allowed set. Prompt: observe -> act -> re-observe to confirm, escalation ladder, no URL-guessing loops, trust one authoritative on-page signal, periodic progress updates. Routing: if a linked resource has a connector, call it; use search for public lookups; open the browser only on explicit intent or connector failure.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: A durable loop with pause/resume/stop exists, but LlmPlanner::from_env returns None unless QUARRY_BROWSER_AGENT_LLM is 1/true/yes (SRC, read in this audit; compose does not set it per baseline), so the default is a deterministic planner. The planner schema offers only navigate/click/type/scroll/wait/extract/done and the system prompt is one short paragraph about ref targeting with no verify, escalation or stop rules (SRC). Connector-first routing between provider actions, Quarry search and the browser is unverified.

approachOriginal: Model Plane execution-core: flip the default behind an org-policy flag, enforce per-run step/time/token budgets, add the versioned procedure prompt and widen the planner schema to Quarry verbs it cannot reach today (press, select, back, get_content), keeping the existing risk gates and ZDR checks. Add a routing policy (connector -> Quarry search/scrape -> browser) recorded in run receipts that honours explicit user intent. Frontend: one 'Do this in the browser' entry point. Evaluate prompt changes against Quarry step receipts.
risks: Runaway cost: budgets are mandatory before default-on. Over-long prompts: keep rules short and test-driven. Eager routing can ignore an explicit request to use the browser.

title: Let users browse freely: a human-session policy plus an omnibox that routes free text to Verevon search
summary: Add a human-browsing session mode distinct from agent runs: an idle-timeout lease (reset by user input and frame activity) instead of max_steps 12 and 120 s, and a broker-defined navigation policy that is not a single-host list, so omnibox entries and link clicks under takeover work. Agent-initiated cross-domain navigation keeps the existing cross_domain_navigation HITL gate, and Quarry's egress/SSRF policy stays on. Add hard reload and make reload retry a failed URL. Rewire browser-omnibox.ts so URL-like input navigates and free text opens Verevon search (Quarry /v1/search results, or Ask into chat), with suggestions from the gateway's existing search autocomplete and local web history.
whyItMatters: A browser locked to its first host for 120 s is not a browser, and today free text in the address bar becomes a google.com URL that the domain lock then rejects. This is the largest day-one usability gap for people, and it is the part of 'a built-in browser users and AI both use' that users touch first.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (navigation commands iab-037; omnibox suggestion service iab-036)
others: Aside (omnibox reuses the browser engine plus an AI mode with attached tabs, aside-browser-product-011)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Navigation controls: 1 of 3 recorded (Codex), table-stakes because Aside is Chromium (INF). Omnibox suggestions: 2 of 3, common.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Commands navigateBack, navigateForward, reload and hardReload (ignore cache); the preload captures mouse buttons 3 and 4; reload from an error page retries the original URL. The suggestion service is token based: start(query) streams matches {contents, description, destinationURL, acceptToken, deleteToken}; accept(token) navigates and records; deleteMatch removes a history entry. For Verevon: a gateway suggest call that merges local history, search autocomplete and URL heuristics, and non-URL input goes to Verevon search rather than google.com.

title: Co-browsing: the agent works in the user's visible session in agent-flagged tabs, with takeover enforced inside Quarry
summary: Phase 1 (S, land in W1): make quarry-edge /step reject agent steps while control_mode is human_takeover (typed USER_TOOK_OVER, monotonic control epoch) and record the initiator (user or agent) in step receipts. Phase 2: an attach mode so a Model Plane run binds to the user's Quarry session through a session-bound child grant and works in a new agent-flagged tab that appears without stealing focus, with Reveal, Take over and Give back. Phase 3: deliverable and handoff tab marks so finished pages stay open for the user.
whyItMatters: Co-browsing is table-stakes in both browser references (Codex and Aside) and is the core of a browser that users and AI share. Today the AI run drives a separate hidden lease that inherits only profile_id and start_url (SRC). T2 re-read the code: takeover is enforced only in the Frontend gateway (browser.rs:705-723 and 2071-2090), and the Quarry /step admission path in agent_routes.rs never consults control_mode (SRC). A Model Plane run that calls Quarry directly is therefore not stopped by a human takeover. This corrects the strength claim (C-t2-08-017) that takeover is authoritative in Quarry.

title: Surface one canonical agent run trace in the UI: typed events, receipts, live view, correlation envelope
summary: Define a versioned TraceEvent envelope owned by the Model Plane ({schema_version, event_id, run_id, occurred_at, producer_seq, correlation{org_id, actor_id, turn_id, request_id, origin}, agent{id, role, parent_id}, type, payload}); have Quarry publish browser-session, step-receipt, egress-decision and artifact events in the same envelope on NATS (persisted unless ZDR), served as GET trace with a cursor plus an SSE tail by from_seq. Gateway proxies the Quarry receipts, egress-receipts, procedure and live-view routes it does not proxy today and the SPA renders one run timeline in place of the FleetRunConsole placeholder; fix the run-start grant/bearer wiring first. Quarry edge adopts x-request-id through a tower layer and an origin enum on runs, and the devtools route gains level/substring filters with a read-only browser.console model tool.
whyItMatters: This is what users watch while the agent browses. Without it, "the Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects" is invisible, approvals lack context and support cannot follow one run across gateway, Model Plane, Quarry and audit. It blocks the vision of a browser shared by humans and AI, and most server-side pieces already exist.

Edge middleware reads x-request-id (or generates it), puts it in the span and response header and forwards it on every internal call. Console pull: a bounded per-tab ring buffer exposed as GET .../console?levels=warn,error&filter=substr&limit=N.

title: Actionability checks and trusted input for every ref-targeted action, then rich input actions
summary: Change Quarry's ref-targeted click/type path from element.click() via Runtime.callFunctionOn to: scroll into view, wait for attached/visible/enabled/stable (poll content quads over two frames), hit-test the centre via DOM.getNodeForLocation including cross-process iframe hops, then dispatch trusted Input.dispatchMouseEvent/KeyEvent. title: Scoped, robots-compliant crawl: wire CrawlFrontier scoping, robots enforcement and typed denials into the live crawl path
summary: The Go CrawlJobWF enqueues every discovered link with no scope or robots check (workflows.go:396-610, SRC), while the Rust CrawlFrontier with typed denials and the RobotsCache/parser exist unused; robots.txt is applied only in /v1/map. Add the scoping vocabulary (include/exclude paths with ReDoS and size caps, subdomain and external-link switches, depth, sitemap mode) on a ScrapeOptions-backed CrawlRequest; enforce robots by default on crawl, batch and Model-proposed autonomous fetches, with ignore-robots as an audited Control Plane entitlement; report blocked URLs as typed per-URL errors with fix-it messages; and decide the ZDR posture of the durable orchestrator path (crawls are refused under ZDR today).
whyItMatters: Scoping and robots compliance are table-stakes in both crawl benchmarks (Firecrawl SRC, Apify DOC). Repo docs claim robots handling is closed while the code does not enforce it (SRC). Unscoped crawls waste budget and expose every org to compliance risk.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: filter_links(candidates, opts) returns (allowed, denials{url: reason}). Checks in order: parse, protocol, fragment-only, depth > maxDiscoveryDepth, scope (directory prefix of seed unless crawlEntireDomain/allowBackwardLinks), domain/subdomain/external, include then exclude patterns on path or full URL, file extension, social-media, robots. Patterns are validated with ReDoS caps (<=1000 patterns, <=2000 chars each, 100k total). Each denial reason maps to a message that names the matched pattern or depth and the option to set (for example allowSubdomains). Apify adds a transformRequest hook so callers can drop or retag requests. || Merged items add: CrawlRequest {url, includePaths[], excludePaths[] (regex, optionally matched on the full URL), maxDiscoveryDepth, limit, crawlEntireDomain, allowSubdomains, allowExternalLinks, sitemap skip|include|only, ignoreQueryParameters, delay, maxConcurrency, scrapeOptions, webhook}; reject over 1000 patterns or 2000 chars each; the frontier filters candidates through scope rules, a robots cache, canonicalisation and dedupe; a robots override exists only behind a team flag; limit is clamped to remaining credits. || Before enqueue/fetch, get robots.txt for the origin from a cache (TTL about 1 day), fetching it through the normal engine chain with a short timeout. Evaluate it for the product user agent. If disallowed, skip the URL and record {url, reason: robots} in a per-job blocked set that the errors endpoint returns. Crawl enforces by default and scrape is opt-in. Override flags (ignore robots, custom UA) are team entitlements checked at request time and forbidden under a compliance profile.
